title: Attention saturation and prefix replay eval
summary: Quick summary: This doc reports on a focused set of onboarding evals aimed at uncovering attention memory saturation, prefix replay behavior, and retrieval fidelity degradation across 8k / 32k / 128k contexts. Tests combine synthetic attention-sink patterns and noisy retrievals to surface regressions vs baseline. Key takeaways: attention saturation manifests as latency and quality regressions under prolonged cross-attention to many retrieved passages; KV-cache warm/replay reduces re-attention costs but interacts poorly with some quantized kernels; noisy retrieval above ~15% degrades grounding and increases hallucination rate.
motivation: We need to certify model variants for serving in Dedicated and Hosted with long-context workloads. Previous onboarding runs focused on truncation thresholds and single-query retrieval fidelity; this pass stresses attention dynamics over prolonged sessions and when retrievals change across turns. Goal: identify deterministic failure modes we can detect in pre-deploy regression and produce actionable mitigations (kernel selection, cache policies, prompt hygiene).
experiment_overview: Variants: baseline-v1.4 (fp16), onboarding-v2.0 (mixed-precision FP16 w/opt kernels), q4_0 and q8_0 quantized builds. Context lengths: 8k, 32k, 128k. Tests: 1) steady-state retrieval stream: 50 turn conversation with 3 retrieved docs per turn; 2) attention-sink injection: repeated near-duplicate long tokens inserted to force large attention matrices; 3) prefix-replay: re-attaching earlier prefixes to measure KV-cache replay vs re-attend cost; 4) truncation edge probes: controlled growth until output truncation occurs. Retrieval noise sweep: 0%, 5%, 15%, 30% spurious items. Each combination run 10 seeds. Latency measured p50/p95; quality measured via reference-based ROUGE/EM for factual tasks and a custom grounding-score for retrieval use.
datasets_and_prompts:
Prompt suites used (short descriptions):
- legal-chron: 120 doc pairs (multi-doc Q/A) simulating legal history, long context required for cross-doc reasoning.
- multi-doc-sum: 200 multi-article summarization prompts that reference facts across >10k tokens.
- kb-recall: 400 single-turn retrieval grounding prompts with ground-truth passages; used to compute retrieval fidelity.
- chat-stream: synthetic 50-turn sessions where user switches topics every 6 turns.
Each prompt set was combined with retrieval corpora sized 1k/10k/50k to vary accidental near-duplicates. Retriever simulated with controlled precision/recall to inject noise levels stated above.
metrics_and_thresholds:
Primary metrics and alert thresholds used in this eval: 
- Grounding-F1 (retrieval fidelity): threshold pass >= 0.82 for onboarding (baseline 0.85).
- Truncation-point index: token index where final answer token-level overlap drops >10% vs unconstrained run.
- Latency: p95 must be <= 1.6x baseline for 8k/32k, <=2.2x for 128k.
- Attention-saturation signal: sustained attention-matrix memory usage growth > 80% of process RSS for >30s flagged.
- KV-cache hit-effectiveness: improvement in token compute for prefix-replay runs must be >= 12% for cache to be considered effective.
- Hallucination-rate: fraction of answers with unsupported assertions; onboarding risk threshold 0.06 (6%).
results_highlights:
High-level findings (ranked by severity):
1) Attention saturation observed on 128k long-lived chats when retrievals contain many long passages (~>30% of tokens from retrieved docs). Symptoms: p95 latency increases 2.4x, and grounding-F1 drops 9-12 points for onboarding-v2.0.
2) KV-cache prefix-replay reduces compute and improves consistency for repeated prefixes — measured 18% token compute reduction on average — but in q4_0 builds we observed mismatch in key ordering leading to occasional token-drop artifacts (3% of runs).
3) Noisy retrievals: at >=15% spurious retrieved passages, hallucination-rate increases markedly; multi-doc-sum tasks showed largest sensitivity (hallucination +11%).
4) Truncation behavior: onboarding-v2.0 shifts truncation-point earlier by ~1.4k tokens in some 128k runs compared to baseline-v1.4, driven primarily by attention reallocation to late retrieved passages.
5) Attention-sinks: artificially duplicated long prefixes cause transient attention spikes but are largely mitigated by dynamic kernel selection in fp16; quantized variants show persistent slowdowns.
6) Quality vs latency tradeoffs: enabling prefix-drop heuristics (drop retrieved docs older than N turns) recovers latency but at a measured grounding-F1 cost of ~3 points; this is acceptably small for many interactive apps but not for legal-chron.
regression_analysis:
Regression summary comparing baseline-v1.4 -> onboarding-v2.0 across key tasks (aggregated across seeds):
- legal-chron grounding-F1: baseline 0.86 -> onboarding 0.77 (regression -0.09)
- multi-doc-sum ROUGE-L: baseline 42.1 -> onboarding 38.6 (regression -3.5)
- kb-recall EM: baseline 0.88 -> onboarding 0.84 (regression -0.04)
- average p95 latency (128k): baseline 1.0s per 1k tokens -> onboarding 2.4s per 1k tokens (worst-case spots)
Notes: regressions localize to runs with high retrieval density and to quantized kernel paths. We classified regressions as "critical" where grounding-F1 drop >0.07 or hallucination-rate jump >0.05; by that rule, 17% of onboarding-v2.0 runs are critical on the legal-chron set.
failure_modes_notes:
Observed failure modes with examples and quick diagnostic signals:
- KV-order-mismatch (q4_0): example run id trace-2025-11-20-128k-3 shows token skipping on token 14207; signal: sudden drop in token-generation probability with KV-cache hit rate still high.
- Attention-sink runaway: repeated near-duplicate paragraphs cause attention memory growth; signal: sustained RSS increase + p95 latency spike.
- Retrieval-noise-induced hallucination: when a spurious passage contradicts gold, model prefers spurious facts after >3 turns; signal: grounding-F1 drop over turns.
- Truncation drift: model begins allocating context to late retrievals causing early truncation of prompt-critical content; signal: final-answer overlap metric trending down as context grows.
recommended_next_steps:
Engineering + Research action items: 
1) Blocker for launch: fix q4_0 KV-ordering bug; assigned to Ravi (JIRA-MLINF-789). Estimated 1 sprint.
2) Add microbench: 10k-step attention-saturation harness (deterministic) to CI for quant builds; return early on memory growth >75%.
3) Add a regression gate: onboarding scans must pass grounding-F1 delta <= -0.05 vs baseline on legal-chron to proceed to Dedicated.
4) Runtime mitigation: implement prefix-age based retrieval trimming policy (configurable per route) and measure effect in next run.
5) Product: document acceptable degradation envelopes per workload (interactive vs archival).
6) Follow-up eval: run with real retriever logs from two customers to validate noise assumptions (target: 2 customers in next month).
raw_observations:
Notes from runs and slack: 
- run logs: trace-2025-11-20-128k-3 had KV misalignment at 14.2k token mark; see slack thread #applied-ml for raw stack traces.
- weirdness: one seed of q8_0 produced near-perfect grounding on multi-doc-sum (likely lucky alignment), flagged as outlier.
- rough timings: 128k runs average 3.1 hours per seed on p4d-like machine; 32k runs ~40 minutes.
- config snippets: retrieval window=3, prefix_keep_turns=8 for most tests; turned prefix_keep_turns=0 for prefix-drop ablation.
